conviction_note: The findings add up to a small positive (+1.1). Acadia has raised or narrowed its 2026 FFO As Adjusted guide at every print this year (1.21-1.25 to 1.22-1.26 to 1.24-1.26), and the stock rose +2.1% and +2.2% on the last two. Consensus of $0.31 for Q3, and $1.24 for the year, sits at or below the low end of the guide. Peers KIM (10-29) and FRT (10-30) raised their outlooks. Against that, every company-level fact found is already public: the 9/14 update, the guide and the peer prints. The drawdown since July follows the 10-year yield above 5.27%, not anything company-specific, so p_up is only 56 on a 2.8% abs move: (0.12 x 2.8) = +0.34. The gap to impact_sum (+1.1) reflects that each small positive is real but mostly priced, and the scaled number carries that uncertainty.
bar: Q3 2026 FFO As Adjusted around $0.31/share. Sources: KeyCorp forecast $0.31 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/what-is-keycorps-forecast-for-akr-q3-earnings-2026-08-19/, 2026-08-19; the page itself only rendered unrelated headlines when fetched, so this rests on the search snippet) and Benzinga's table $0.31 with revenue $98.8M (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/AKR/earnings-forecasts). FY2026 consensus is $1.24 per snippet. The company guide is FY2026 FFO As Adjusted $1.24-$1.26 (8-K ex99.1, 2026-07-28, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000899629/000119312526321040/akr-ex99_1.htm). With H1 at $0.61 ($0.30 Q1 + $0.31 Q2), that implies H2 of $0.63-0.65, or about $0.315-0.325 a quarter. Consensus therefore sits at the bottom of the guide-implied range. The bar comes from the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, so it is not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest was 13,361,699 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 9.7% of 137.3M shares outstanding, with 10.42 days to cover. It is down from a 21.59M peak on 2026-06-15 and was 14.05M on 9-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/akr/shortinterest). No usable option chain (baseline options status no_paired_strikes), so there is no skew. An Unusual Whales snippet quoting a ±10.4% implied move is not credible against a 21% realised vol and the absent chain, and is ignored. Run-up: +1.6% over 5 days, +2.4% over 20 days, 16% below the 52-week high. That follows a 22.47 (July) to 18.74 (September) slide during a sector-wide rate selloff.

findings.finding: Acadia has lifted its 2026 FFO As Adjusted guide at every print this year: $1.21-1.25 originally, then $1.22-1.26 on 4/28, then $1.24-1.26 on 7/28. H1 was $0.61 (Q1 $0.30, Q2 $0.31 against $0.30 consensus). The guide implies H2 of $0.63-0.65, while Q3 consensus is $0.31 and FY consensus $1.24, the low end. So a Q3 of $0.31-0.32 plus a guide narrowed toward $1.25-1.26 is the likeliest release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide raise with a beat on 2026-07-28 drew +2.21%; the guide raise on 2026-04-28 drew +2.12%. The FY2025 Q4 print on 2026-02-10, an EPS miss per secondary sources, drew -4.15%. The Q3 2025 print (2025-10-28) drew -0.16%. Seven-print median |move| is 2.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has not moved off the low end of the guide ($1.24 FY), so the street is not modelling another narrowing toward the top. If it were, FY consensus would sit at $1.25-1.26 and Q3 at $0.32. The stock is also 16% off its July high despite the guide raise, which fits a rate-driven discount rather than an expectation of further raises. Caveat built into the size: Q3 itself lands inside the guided range, so only an upward narrowing adds anything.
findings.independence: Q1 guide and result: 8-K ex99.1 2026-04-28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000899629/000119312526187104/akr-ex99_1.htm). The consensus figure comes from different sources (Benzinga, KeyCorp via MarketBeat).

findings.finding: The 2026-09-14 intra-quarter update reported $119M of Q3 REIT street-retail acquisitions (Greene St $60M, Bleecker $20M, Greenwich Ave $10M, Melrose $29M) and $742M YTD across the REIT and investment management. It also reported 12 new Q3 leases worth $4.8M ABR at share ($3.8M street retail), double-digit cash spreads, and 129 Fifth Ave leased within 30 days above underwriting at a yield on cost above 9%. No new equity was issued and about $352M of forward proceeds remain. Q3 operations were tracking the plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Leasing spreads and same-property NOI (+8.7% in Q2, street retail +15.6%) were the headline of the July print, which drew +2.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, so mostly priced. What is not priced is how the leases and the $16.5M signed-not-open pipeline (Q2 release) convert into Q4 run-rate and 2027 commentary. The stock fell through September despite this update, during a sector rate selloff, which suggests the market treated company news as secondary to the 10-year yield.
findings.independence: Commercial Observer on the Greene St purchase (https://commercialobserver.com/2026/09/acadia-buys-soho-69-71-greene-street/). Same company as finding 1 but a different document.

findings.finding: Shopping-center peers that reported in the week before the print raised their outlooks. Kimco (10-29) raised its 2026 outlook on record 96.6% occupancy and Q3 FFO of $0.47 vs $0.44. Federal Realty (10-30) raised and tightened Core FFO to $7.54-7.58 from $7.48-7.56, with 14% cash leasing spreads and its leased rate up 40bp. Retail tenant demand was healthy into Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of AKR moving on peer prints. AKR's street-retail mix (Q2 SP NOI +15.6% street) is more levered to luxury and urban tenants than KIM or FRT.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: both prints were out before AKR's 10-30 close. It is filed as a sector proxy confirming no tenant-credit surprise. If the market had worried about AKR-specific demand, AKR would have lagged peers after their prints. Instead its 5-day run-up is +1.6%.
findings.independence: Kimco Q3 2026 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000879101/000119312526436941/kim-ex99_1.htm), 2026-10-29. A proxy, not AKR's own number.

findings.finding: Short interest was 13.36M shares on 2026-10-15, about 9.7% of 137.3M shares outstanding, with 10.4 days to cover on a stock trading about 1.1M shares a day. A clean print with a guide narrowed upward meets a short base that needs ten sessions to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest fell from 21.6M (June) to 12.0M (August) around the July beat-and-raise, which drew +2.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: Days to cover above 10 is an amplifier rather than a direction. It matters only if the print is clean, and the baseline (no option chain) carries no positioning statement at all.

findings.finding: AKR's drawdown from $22.47 (July) to $18.74 (September) coincided with the 10-year Treasury yield reaching 5.27% at the end of September, its highest in about 25 years, and REITs falling 5.7% in September. It is a sector rate move, not a company-specific cause. Rates over the window are a two-sided risk the print cannot settle.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: this explains the drawdown and does not predict the print. It is filed so the judges can see the drawdown has a non-company cause.

findings.finding: About $352M of unsettled forward equity remains (17.8M shares / $369M at 6/30 per the Q2 release; $352M at 9/14). It funds the REIT acquisition pipeline and the Henderson Ave development, 'fully funded, on a forward basis'. The money buys street-retail assets leasing at double-digit spreads and a yield on cost above 9%, so this is funding a visible ramp, not distress. Settlement dilution is a 2027 per-share question rather than a Q3 one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 $200M forward offering came in the same quarter as the guide raise; the stock rose +2.21% on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: Known and disclosed. Answering what the money buys (accretive street retail with corroborating leasing) signs this at zero.
findings.independence: The 9/14 update (https://earningswhispers.com/article/AKR/2609143342) confirms no new equity in Q3 and $352M remaining. That shares a company with findings 1 and 2.

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 release moves to before the open on 11-02 with an 11:00 ET call the same day; all seven prior prints were after the close. This shortens the window in which the release is digested before the scored close.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior bmo prints in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: Not directional. It means the full call is inside the scored session, so the reaction should be more complete than after a pre-market-only digestion.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The small positive lean sits against a stock 16% off its high with a modest +2.4% 20-day run-up, which is consistent with a rate-driven discount rather than priced disappointment.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guided range): the guidance finding went from +0.6 to +0.5, since Q3 lands inside the guide and only an upward narrowing adds anything. The bar was verified against the company guide plus two agreeing estimates, so no cap.
Lesson 6 / core table (already public, inside the guide): the intra-quarter update finding went from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 5 (a proxy is sized small): the peer read-through went from +0.3 to +0.2, since KIM and FRT were already printed before the 10-30 close.
Lesson 7: short interest is an amplifier, not a direction; the positioning finding went from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): forward equity funds accretive street-retail acquisitions with corroborating leasing, so it went from -0.1 to 0.0.
